reference: F. Najman, degree-10 torsion computations (2026), unpublished. Sporadicity: Derickx-Sutherland, Theorem 4.1; Najman-Varivoda, Table 1.
notes: First representative. One representative per isomorphism class of (K,E), following the census verifier convention. The two representatives are 2-isogenous over the same decic field and arise from the two marking orbits of degree-5 points on X1(3,18) over Q(zeta_3). The points P and Q have independent exact orders 3 and 18. Both curves have exact full torsion C3 x C18: good unramified residue-degree-2 reductions at 7 have exactly 54 points over F49, independently verified in Magma and Sage. Sporadicity follows from rank zero over Q(zeta_3) (Derickx-Sutherland, Theorem 4.1) and gonality at least 6 (Najman-Varivoda, Table 1), strictly greater than the relative degree 5; thus there are finitely many points of absolute degree at most 10.
